vsm2.19:16.1: Another fourfold classification of kamma is this: productive, consolidating, frustrating, and supplanting.
vsm2.19:16.2: Herein, (ix) what is called productive is both profitable and unprofitable.
vsm2.19:16.3: It produces the material and immaterial aggregates both at rebirth-linking and during the course of an existence.
vsm2.19:16.4:
(x) Consolidating kamma cannot produce result, but when result has already been produced in the provision
of rebirth-linking by other kamma, it consolidates the pleasure or pain that arises and makes it last.
vsm2.19:16.5:
(xi) And when result has already been produced in the provision of rebirth-linking by other kamma,
frustrating kamma frustrates and obstructs the pleasure or pain that arises and does not allow it to last.
vsm2.19:16.6:
(xii) Supplanting kamma is itself both profitable and unprofitable; and it supplants other, weaker kamma,
prevents its resulting and usurps that kamma’s opportunity in order to cause its own result.
vsm2.19:16.7: But when the opportunity has thus been furnished by the other kamma, it is that supplanting kamma’s result that is called arisen.
vsm2.19:17.1:
The succession of kamma and its result in the twelve classes of kamma is clear in its true nature
only to the Buddhas’ “knowledge of kamma and its result,” which knowledge is not shared by disciples.
vsm2.19:17.2: But the succession of kamma and its result can be known in part by one practicing insight.
vsm2.19:17.3: That is why this explanation of difference in kamma shows only the mere headings.
vsm2.19:17.4:
This is how one man discerns mentality-materiality by means of the round of kamma and the round of kamma-result,
applying this twelve-fold kamma classification to the round of kamma.
vsm2.19:18.1:
When he has thus seen by means of the round of kamma and the round of kamma-result how
mentality-materiality’s occurrence is due to a condition, he sees that as now, so in the past, its occurrence
was due to a condition by means of the round of kamma and the round of kamma-result, and that in the future
its occurrence will be due to a condition by means of the round of kamma and the round of kamma-result.
vsm2.19:18.2:
This is kamma and kamma-result, the round of kamma and the round of kamma-result, the occurrence of kamma and the occurrence
of kamma-result, the continuity of kamma and the continuity of kamma-result, action and the fruit of action:
vsm2.19:18.3:
> Kamma-result proceeds from kamma,
> Result has kamma for its source,
> Future becoming springs from kamma,
> And this is how the world goes round.
vsm2.19:19.1:
When he sees thus, he abandons all his uncertainty, that is to say, the sixteen kinds
described in the way beginning, “Was I in the past?” see §6.
vsm2.19:19.2:
NO DOER APART FROM KAMMA AND RESULT

In all kinds of becoming, generation, destiny, station, and abode there appears only
mentality-materiality, which occurs by means of linking of cause with fruit.
vsm2.19:19.3: He sees no doer over and above the doing, no experiencer of the result over and above the occurrence of the result.
vsm2.19:19.4:
But he sees clearly with right understanding that the wise say “doer” when there is doing and “experiencer”
when there is experiencing simply as a mode of common usage.
vsm2.19:20.1:
Hence the Ancients said:

> There is no doer of a deed
> Or one who reaps the deed’s result;
> Phenomena alone flow on—
> No other view than this is right.
vsm2.19:20.2:
> And so, while kamma and result
> Thus causally maintain their round,
> As seed and tree succeed in turn,
> No first beginning can be shown.

> Nor in the future round of births
> Can they be shown not to occur:
vsm2.19:20.3:
> Sectarians, not knowing this,
> Have failed to gain self-mastery. > They assume a being, see it as
> Eternal or annihilated.
> Adopt the sixty-two wrong views,
> Each contradicting one another.
vsm2.19:20.4:
> The stream of craving bears them on
> Caught in the meshes of their views:
> And as the stream thus bears them on
> They are not freed from suffering.
vsm2.19:20.5:
> A monk, disciple of the Buddha,
> With direct knowledge of this fact
> Can penetrate this deep and subtle
> Void conditionality.
vsm2.19:20.6:
> There is no kamma in result,
> Nor does result exist in kamma;
> Though they are void of one another,
> There is no fruit without the kamma.
vsm2.19:20.7:
> As fire does not exist inside
> The sun, a gem, cow-dung, nor yet
> Outside them, but is brought to be
> By means of its component parts,
vsm2.19:20.8:
> So neither can result be found
> Within the kamma, nor without;
> Nor does the kamma still persist
> In the result it has produced.
vsm2.19:20.10:
> For here there is no Brahmā God,
> Creator of the round of births,
> Phenomena alone flow on—
> Cause and component their condition.
vsm2.19:21.1:
FULL-UNDERSTANDING OF THE KNOWN

When he has discerned the conditions of mentality-materiality in this way by means of the round of kamma
and the round of kamma-result, and has abandoned uncertainty about the three periods of time, then all past,
future and present states are understood by him in accordance with death and rebirth-linking.
vsm2.19:21.2: This is his full-understanding of the known (see XX.3).
vsm2.19:22.1: He understands thus: “Aggregates produced in the past with kamma as condition ceased there too.
vsm2.19:22.2:
But other aggregates are produced in this becoming with past kamma as their condition, although there
is no single thing that has come over from the past becoming to this becoming.
vsm2.19:22.3:
And aggregates produced in this becoming with kamma as their condition will
cease. And in the future becoming other aggregates will be produced,
vsm2.19:22.4: although no single thing will go over from this becoming to the future becoming.
vsm2.19:22.5:
“Furthermore, just as, while the recitation from the teacher’s mouth does not enter into the pupil’s mouth,
yet recitation does not because of that fail to take place in the pupil’s mouth—
vsm2.19:22.6:
and while the potion drunk by the proxy does not enter the sick man’s stomach,
yet the sickness does not because of that fail to be cured—
vsm2.19:22.7:
and while the arrangement of the ornaments on the face does not pass over to the reflection of the face in the looking
glass, yet the arrangement of the ornaments does not because of that fail to appear—
vsm2.19:22.8:
and while the flame of a lamp does not move over from one wick to another,
yet the flame does not because of that fail to be produced—
vsm2.19:22.9: so too, while nothing whatever moves over from the past becoming to this becoming, or from this to the future becoming,
vsm2.19:22.10:
yet aggregates, bases, and elements do not fail to be produced here with aggregates, bases, and elements in the past
becoming as their condition, or in the future becoming with aggregates, bases, and elements here as their condition.”
vsm2.19:23.1:
> Just as eye-consciousness comes next
> Following on mind element,
> Which, though it does not come from that,
> Yet fails not next to be produced,
vsm2.19:23.2:
> So too, in rebirth-linking, conscious
> Continuity takes place:
> The prior consciousness breaks up,
> The subsequent is born from that.
vsm2.19:23.3:
> They have no interval between,
> Nor gap that separates the two;
> While naught whatever passes over,
> Still rebirth-linking comes about.
vsm2.19:24.1:
When all states are understood by him thus in accordance with death and rebirth-linking,
his knowledge of discerning the conditions of mentality-materiality is sound in all its aspects
vsm2.19:24.2: and the sixteen kinds of doubt are more effectively abandoned.
vsm2.19:24.3:
And not only that, but the eight kinds of doubt that occur in the way beginning thus,
“He is doubtful about the Master” (A III 248; Dhs §1004) are abandoned too,
vsm2.19:24.4: and the sixty-two kinds of views are suppressed (See DN 1 and MN 102).
vsm2.19:25.1:
The knowledge that has been established by the overcoming of doubt about the three periods of time by discerning
the conditions of mentality-materiality according to the various methods should be understood as “purification by overcoming doubt.”
vsm2.19:25.2: Other terms for it are “knowledge of the relations of states” and “correct knowledge” and “right vision.”
vsm2.19:26.1:
For this is said: “Understanding of discernment of conditions thus, ‘Ignorance is a condition, formations are conditionally
arisen, and both these states are conditionally arisen,’ is knowledge of the causal relationship of states” (Paṭis I 50).
vsm2.19:26.2:
And: “When he brings to mind as impermanent, what states does he correctly know and see? How is there right seeing?
How, by inference from that, are all formations clearly seen as impermanent? Wherein is doubt abandoned?
vsm2.19:26.3:
When he brings to mind as painful … When he brings to mind as not-self, what states
does he correctly know and see? … Wherein is doubt abandoned?
vsm2.19:26.4:
“When he brings to mind as impermanent, he correctly knows and sees the sign. Hence ‘right seeing’ is said.
Thus, by inference from that, all formations are clearly seen as impermanent. Herein doubt is abandoned.
vsm2.19:26.5:
When he brings to mind as painful, he correctly knows and sees occurrence. Hence … When he brings to mind
as not-self, he correctly knows and sees the sign and occurrence. Hence ‘right seeing’ is said.
vsm2.19:26.6: Thus, by inference from that, all states are clearly seen as not-self. Herein doubt is abandoned.
vsm2.19:26.7:
“Correct knowledge and right seeing and overcoming of doubt —are these things different in meaning
and different in the letter or are they one in meaning and only the letter is different?
vsm2.19:26.8:
Correct knowledge and right seeing and overcoming of doubt—these things
are one in meaning and only the letter is different” (Paṭis II 62f.).
vsm2.19:27.1:
When a man practicing insight has become possessed of this knowledge, he has found comfort in the Buddhas’ Dispensation,
he has found a foothold, he is certain of his destiny, he is called a “lesser stream-enterer.”
vsm2.19:27.2:
> So would a bhikkhu overcome
> His doubts, then ever mindfully
> Let him discern conditions both
> Of mind and matter thoroughly.
vsm2.19:27.3:
The nineteenth chapter called “The Description of
Purification by Overcoming Doubt” in the Treatise on the
Development of Understanding in the Path of Purification
composed for the purpose of gladdening good people.
